items.period: Shang oracle-script style; modern redraw, not a dated artifact specimen
items.caption: A Shang oracle-script style redraw of 好. Its upper looped figure is larger than the branching figure below, a contrast relevant to the proposed 女-plus-子 analysis; the redraw alone does not establish the figures’ identities or the character’s original motivation.
items.alt: Black glyph with a large looped upper figure and a smaller branching lower figure, connected by a horizontal stroke.
items.selection_reason: Shows a reported early configuration and size contrast relevant to the conventional 女-plus-子 analysis, while leaving the proposed original motivation unresolved.
items.rights: Wikimedia Commons file page states public-domain status for the SVG representation and also reports permission from Richard Sears; retain attribution/provenance as shown on the file page.

items.period: Bronze-script style; no specific specimen date established
items.tradition: Bronze inscription script; modern vector redraw
items.caption: A bronze-script style redraw of 好, with a tall branching figure on the left and a rounded figure on the right. Early forms are reported with 女 and 子 in variable positions; this form does not establish a sequence of change.
items.alt: Black glyph with a tall branching left figure and a rounded, open right-hand figure.
items.selection_reason: Adds a contrasting arrangement that helps illustrate reported variation in component placement without implying chronological succession.
items.rights: Wikimedia Commons file page states public-domain status for the SVG representation and also reports permission from Richard Sears; retain attribution/provenance as shown on the file page.

limitations.text: The original motivation of 好 remains unresolved. Proposed explanations include mother–child affection, a woman’s beauty, and affection between a man and a woman; cited early uses do not directly attest the mother–child interpretation.
These are modern redrawings labeled by script tradition, not photographs of dated inscriptions. They illustrate reported forms and variation but do not establish a verified chronological sequence.
